auditor_value: (rod taken horizontal) T = mg/(2 sin37°) = 50/3 ≈ 16.67 N; hinge H_x = T cos37° = 40/3 ≈ 13.33 N (away from the wall), H_y = mg − T sin37° = 10 N (up); resultant = 50/3 ≈ 16.67 N

findings.quote: Using the full rod length 4 m as the moment arm for the weight instead of the midpoint distance 2 m, which halves the found tension.
findings.note: With the weight's arm taken as 4 m the moment equation becomes T sin37° × 4 = 20 × 4, so T = 33.33 N — the tension DOUBLES, it does not halve. The stated cause cannot produce the effect the text names.
findings.fix: Using the full rod length 4 m as the moment arm for the weight instead of the midpoint distance 2 m, which doubles the found tension to 33.33 N.

findings.quote: Swapping sin37° and cos37° when finding the hinge components, giving H_x = 10 N and H_y = 13.33 N.
findings.note: Swapping sine and cosine in the two hinge equations gives H_x = T sin37° = 10 N and H_y = 20 − T cos37° = 6.67 N; the value 13.33 N for H_y does not follow from the stated cause.
findings.fix: Swapping sin37° and cos37° when finding the hinge components, giving H_x = 10 N and H_y = 6.67 N.

question_defect: Neither the question text nor the figure description says the rod is horizontal; the tension depends on the rod's inclination (moment arm of the weight). The solution states its assumption ('The rod is horizontal') in steps[0], which is acceptable handling.
notes: Independent solve (rod horizontal) matches T = 16.67 N, H_x = 13.33 N, H_y = 10 N, resultant 16.67 N. All five step equations follow. Only the two mistake entries are defective, each on the number it names.
